newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INDUSTRY UNIONS SAY BUFFERS NEEDED IN EMU.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INDUSTRY UNIONS SAY BUFFERS NEEDED IN EMU.

text.p: Key unions said in a joint resolution on Thursday that the Finnish economy is so different from economies elsewhere in Europe that national buffers will be necessary to cope with shocks if Finland joins EMU.

The delegation of industrial unions led by metal workers' chairman Per-Erik Lundh said in a statement that national stabilisation tools will be needed to offset the loss of economic policy means resulting from Finnish EMU-membership.
The 14-union strong delegation groups all key export sector unions and represents over 600,000 organised workers. Lundh is among Finland's most influential trade union leaders.
"The structure of the Finnish economy differs substantially from the economies of countries in central Europe and our economic development may turn out different," the unions said.
"A shock affecting our one-sided economy will not affect European monetary or economic policy," they said in the statement.

"Instead of the economic policy arsenal of tools lost in EMU we will need national economic stabilisers to soften blows hurting industry in a disturbance and to prevent problems from spreading throughout the national economy," they said.
The government should investigate which kind of buffer arrangements would be best suited reduce the economy's sensitivity to cyclical fluctuations and disturbances.
"Significant benefits can be achieved for companies, employees and the entire national economy by developing funds and conditions for reserves," the unions said.

Funds should collect contributions from "good earnings" during cyclical upswings and "curb inflation pressures by cutting sharp growth in income," they said. The funds should secure workers' income when a company's ability to pay wages weakens, they added.
In addition to various ways of piling up funds for bleaker times, the industrial unions said it was necessary to strengthen the Finnish collective bargaining system. It did not elaborate.
